ideas: Sharing ideas and getting better solutions
Focus and freedom when working alone

phrases.meaning: teach and learn from one another
someone who works well with others

model: I prefer working in a team, although I can work independently when I need to. First, teamwork usually leads to better ideas. When I get stuck on a problem, I can bounce ideas off my colleagues, and a fresh pair of eyes often spots something I've missed. For example, I've been working on a new website design for a client this month, and I'd been struggling with the homepage for days. Then a teammate suggested a simpler layout in a five-minute chat, and the client loved it. Another reason is that people in a team bring different strengths, so we can share the workload and learn from each other. I've learned a lot about data analysis just by sitting next to a colleague who's brilliant with spreadsheets. I've never had to do a big project completely alone, and honestly, I don't think I'd enjoy it as much. So overall, I'd describe myself as a team player, and I'd always choose working with others.
